_meta.indication: CABENUVA is indicated as a complete regimen for treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable regimen with no history of treatment failure and no known/suspected resistance to cabotegravir or rilpivirine.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, noninferiority trial with a 20-week dolutegravir induction phase; virologically suppressed subjects randomized 1:1 to CAB+RPV (oral lead-in then Q4W injections) or remain on current ARV regimen.
pivotal_trials.population: HIV-1-infected, antiretroviral therapy-naive adults who became virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) after 20-week dolutegravir induction.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with plasma HIV-1 RNA >=50 copies/mL at Week 48.
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 48, 2% of CAB+RPV vs 2% CAR had HIV-1 RNA >=50 copies/mL; treatment difference -0.4% (95% CI: -2.8%, 2.1%), demonstrating noninferiority.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, noninferiority switch trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to switch to oral CAB+RPV (oral lead-in then Q4W injections) or remain on current ARV regimen.
pivotal_trials.population: HIV-1-infected, ART-experienced, virologically suppressed adults (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable regimen for at least 6 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with plasma HIV-1 RNA >=50 copies/mL at Week 48.
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 48, 2% of CAB+RPV vs 1% CAR had HIV-1 RNA >=50 copies/mL; treatment difference 0.7% (95% CI: -1.2%, 2.5%), demonstrating noninferiority.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were injection site reactions (83% vs 0), pyrexia (8%), fatigue (5%), and headache (4%). Serious safety concerns include hypersensitivity reactions, post-injection reactions, hepatotoxicity, and depressive disorders.
target_moa: Two-drug regimen: cabotegravir, an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI), plus rilpivirine, an HIV-1 non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI).
modality: small molecule (2-drug co-packaged extended-release injectable suspension)

advisory_committee.vote: CAB+RPV was not taken to an FDA advisory committee because no unexpected significant safety or efficacy issues were identified.

description.text: Added new every-2-month gluteal intramuscular dosing regimen of Cabenuva as a complete regimen for HIV-1 treatment in virologically suppressed adults

citations.quote:
- New dosage regimen of every-2-month gluteal intramuscular injections of Cabenuva as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies per mL) on a stable antiretroviral regimen with no history of treatment failure and with no known or suspected resistance to either cabotegravir or rilpivirine
- Updates to ADVERSE REACTIONS, Clinical Trials Experience to include additional safety data as well as injection-associated adverse reactions based on week 48 data from ATLAS-2M
- Updates to CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, Pharmacokinetics and Microbiology section of the labeling with additional pharmacokinetic data for the every-2-month dosage regimen as well as virologic resistance data based on ATLAS-2M data
- Updates to CLINICAL STUDIES, Clinical Trials in Adults for Treatment of HIV-1 infection with new clinical trial data to support the new dosage regimen
- Updates to PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION to provide advice on Cabenuva being administered as a every-2-month dosage regimen after use of lead-in therapy with oral Vocabria and Edurant

summary.text: CABENUVA was a priority review NDA for a novel 2-drug injectable HIV-1 regimen. Efficacy was established in two phase 3 noninferiority trials (FLAIR and ATLAS). The original submission received a Complete Response letter on December 19, 2019 for manufacturing facility deficiencies; the resubmission was approved January 21, 2021 with required pediatric postmarketing studies.
